synopsis: NATM is the UNECE road-vehicle assessment method whose 2022 guidelines define simulation credibility assessment across management, data and model validation, and team expertise; its frameworks require adaptation before off-road use [f15389, f7143, f5112]. Its multi-pillar approach combines credibility-assessed simulation with physical testing: virtual testing covers the operational design domain within a validated envelope, while physical tests validate the toolchain, confirm the system and remain necessary for highest-integrity claims [f1767, f7840, f7841, f10330]. NATM also includes post-release monitoring as its fifth pillar, feeding operational evidence back into the model, although the weighting of scenario-based versus mileage- or exposure-based safety arguments remains contested [f8052, f8234, f7438]. The booklet recommends an R171 Annex 5 or NATM-style credibility package and replacing TRL with M&S credibility frameworks for the validation toolchain; these frameworks suit high uncertainty and fixed deadlines but are described as largely declarative [f2648, f10031, f10027, f10029]. For planning, the credibility approach maps onto machine-model variant management, and NATM is among the recommended sources for a 2–6-page evidence, V&V and test-strategy section [f2561, f10162].
